events.title: God tests Abraham and tells him to offer Isaac
events.narrative_summary: After these things God tests Abraham, calling him by name. He tells him to take Isaac, his only son whom he loves, to the land of Moriah and offer him there as a burnt offering on a mountain that God will show.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: The text says only 'after these things'; no figure is given. Anchored on the birth of Isaac (START of evt.gen_21.sarah_bears_isaac) with an offset of 25 years and a margin of 12 years, so the window is Isaac aged about 13 to 37. Lower bound: Ishmael has been sent away (Gen 21, c. 2064 BCE) and Isaac, a 'lad' (na'ar) who carries the wood, is no infant. Upper bound: Sarah dies at 127 (Gen 23:1), when Isaac is 37 (Abraham 100 at his birth, Gen 21:5; Sarah 90, Gen 17:17), and Gen 23 follows this chapter. Targum Pseudo-Jonathan 22:1 puts Isaac at 36 (bar telatin ve-shit shnin), inside the window. The speech is brief, 10 minutes. MACRO_ERA.

events.title: Abraham rises early and sets out for Moriah
events.narrative_summary: Abraham rises early in the morning, saddles his donkey, takes two young men and Isaac, splits the wood for the burnt offering, and goes toward the place God named.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'Rose early in the morning' is BOKER, taken as the first morning after the command, so the event starts at the end of the command with no offset and snaps to 06:00. Duration is the journey: `urim travel loc.beersheba loc.moriah_mount --mode donkey` gives 70 km straight, c. 88 km by road, 4 km/h, 21.9 h moving, elapsed about 2 days. This agrees with 'on the third day' in 22:4. Margin 2 hours.

events.title: On the third day Abraham sees the place from afar
events.narrative_summary: On the third day Abraham lifts up his eyes and sees the place in the distance.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'On the third day' counted inclusively: the day of departure is day 1, so the sighting falls at the departure START + 2 days; the first BOKER is already the start, so no time_of_day. Margin 12 hours for the Hebrew-day and inclusive-counting ambiguity. It matches the 2-day donkey journey from `urim travel`. Rashi: the delay was to avoid a sudden shock; Radak: the third day since leaving home.

events.title: Abraham tells his servants to wait with the donkey
events.narrative_summary: Abraham tells his young men to stay here with the donkey while he and the boy go on to worship and then return to them.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Continuous with the sighting on the same day: starts when the sighting ends. A short speech, 10 minutes, margin 1 hour. Tier DAY_SEQUENCE, the day the third-day indication frames.

events.title: Abraham and Isaac go up together and speak of the lamb
events.narrative_summary: Abraham lays the wood on Isaac and carries the fire and the knife, and they walk on together. Isaac asks where the lamb is, and Abraham answers that God will provide himself the lamb for the burnt offering.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Continuous after the servants stay behind, the same day. The remaining walk from the point of sighting to the mountain is estimated at 2 hours (the text gives no figure), margin 1 hour. Not an hour of the day, so DAY_SEQUENCE.

events.title: Abraham builds the altar, binds Isaac and takes the knife
events.narrative_summary: At the place, Abraham builds an altar, arranges the wood, binds Isaac and lays him on the altar above the wood. He stretches out his hand and takes the knife to slay his son.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Starts the moment the climb ends. Building an altar, arranging the wood and binding take about an hour; margin 30 minutes. The text names no hour; DAY_SEQUENCE.

events.title: The angel of the LORD calls from heaven and stops Abraham
events.narrative_summary: The angel of the LORD calls Abraham twice by name from heaven and tells him not to lay his hand on the boy, for now God knows that Abraham fears God, since he did not withhold his only son.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: The call interrupts the raised knife, so the event starts when the binding ends, with no delay. Five minutes, margin 5 minutes.

events.title: Abraham offers a ram in place of his son
events.narrative_summary: Abraham lifts his eyes and sees a ram caught by its horns in a thicket. He takes it and offers it as a burnt offering instead of his son, and calls the place 'The LORD will provide'.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Follows the angel's words at once. Taking, killing and burning the ram, then naming the place, is estimated at 2 hours (a rite takes hours); margin 30 minutes. The text gives no hour.

events.title: The angel calls a second time and swears the blessing
events.narrative_summary: The angel of the LORD calls to Abraham from heaven a second time. In the LORD's name he swears that because Abraham did not withhold his only son, he will bless and multiply his offspring like the stars and the sand, and all nations will be blessed through them.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'A second time' follows the first call and the offering; it starts when the ram offering ends. A short speech, 10 minutes, margin 1 hour. The text gives no hour.

events.title: Abraham returns to his servants and they go to Beersheba
events.narrative_summary: Abraham returns to his young men, and they rise and go together to Beersheba, where Abraham lives.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Starts right after the oath. The return is the same distance as the way out: `urim travel loc.beersheba loc.moriah_mount --mode donkey` gave 70 km straight, c. 88 km by road, 4 km/h, elapsed about 2 days. The text gives no duration, so 2 days with a margin of a day. Isaac is not named in the verse.

events.title: Abraham is told that Milcah has borne sons to Nahor
events.narrative_summary: After these things Abraham is told that Milcah has also borne children to his brother Nahor: eight sons, among them Bethuel, who fathered Rebekah, and four more sons by Nahor's concubine Reumah.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'After these things' with no figure. Rashi has the news reach Abraham on his return from Moriah, so it starts at the end of the return with no offset; the margin is a year because the text gives no date and the births themselves are undated. MACRO_ERA.

causal_edges.causal_explanation: Abraham's word 'God will provide himself a lamb' (22:8) comes true when he finds a ram caught in the thicket (22:13).
The angel calls out because Abraham has taken the knife to slay Isaac (22:10–11).
The oath and blessing come 'because you have done this thing and have not withheld your son' (22:16).
Abraham sets out because God commanded him to take Isaac to Moriah (22:3 answers 22:2).

entities.summary_bio: The altar Abraham builds on the mountain God showed him. Isaac is bound on it, and the ram is offered on it in his place.

aliases: the ram caught in the thicket
entities.summary_bio: A ram Abraham finds caught by its horns in a thicket after the angel's call. He offers it as a burnt offering in place of his son, answering his earlier words that God will provide the lamb.

entities.etymology_meaning: Hebrew ma'akhelet, a 'cutting, devouring' blade; the word is used for a slaughtering knife.
entities.summary_bio: The knife Abraham carries with the fire up the mountain. He takes it in hand to slaughter Isaac, until the angel calls out.

entities.canonical_name: The wood for the burnt offering
entities.summary_bio: Wood Abraham splits before setting out. Isaac carries it up the mountain, and Abraham arranges it on the altar beneath the bound Isaac.
Two unnamed servants who go with Abraham and Isaac to Moriah. Abraham leaves them behind with the donkey where he first sees the place from afar, and they later go back with Abraham to Beersheba.

entities.etymology_meaning: Probably 'seen by the LORD' or 'provided by the LORD'; the text itself plays on the verb 'to see' in 22:8, 14.
entities.summary_bio: The region and mountain to which God sends Abraham to offer Isaac. Abraham sees it from afar on the third day, builds the altar there and names the place 'The LORD will provide'.

entities.etymology_meaning: Probably 'height' or 'highland'; the same name as the people and region of Aram.
entities.summary_bio: Son of Kemuel and grandson of Nahor, named only in the genealogy of Nahor's household. A different Aram from the son of Shem in GEN.10.
Second son of Nahor and Milcah, brother of Uz, and a nephew of Abraham.

entities.etymology_meaning: Uncertain; possibly linked to the Chaldeans (Kasdim).
entities.summary_bio: A son of Nahor and Milcah and a nephew of Abraham.
A son of Nahor and his concubine Reumah, and a nephew of Abraham.
A son of Nahor and Milcah and a nephew of Abraham.

entities.etymology_meaning: Meaning uncertain; perhaps 'he weeps' or 'he drips'.
entities.summary_bio: A son of Nahor and Milcah and a nephew of Abraham.

entities.etymology_meaning: Probably 'raised by God' or 'assembly of God'.
entities.summary_bio: A son of Nahor and Milcah, described as the father of Aram. A nephew of Abraham.
The youngest-named son of Nahor and his concubine Reumah, and a nephew of Abraham. The same name appears later for other people.
A son of Nahor and Milcah and a nephew of Abraham.
Concubine of Nahor, Abraham's brother. She bore him four sons: Tebah, Gaham, Tahash and Maacah.

entities.etymology_meaning: Probably a kind of animal ('badger' or 'seacow'), as in the name of the tabernacle covering.
entities.summary_bio: A son of Nahor and his concubine Reumah, and a nephew of Abraham.
A son of Nahor and his concubine Reumah, and a nephew of Abraham.

entities.etymology_meaning: Uncertain; possibly 'counsel' or tied to the land of Uz.
entities.summary_bio: Firstborn son of Nahor and Milcah, so a nephew of Abraham. Named in the report brought to Abraham after Moriah.

components.evidence_explanation: GEN.22.12: 'now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your son, your only son, from me'.
GEN.22.1: 'God put Abraham to the test'; the test ends when the angel says 'now I know that you fear God' (22.12).
GEN.22.9: Abraham bound Isaac and laid him on the altar; GEN.22.12 forbids the harm and ends the state.
GEN.22.14: Abraham called the name of that place 'The LORD will provide', and it is said to this day 'on the mount of the LORD it shall be provided'.
GEN.22.24: 'his concubine, whose name was Reumah, bore also Tebah, Gaham, Tahash and Maacah'.

components.label_value: Sworn blessing and seed to Abraham
components.evidence_explanation: GEN.22.16-18: 'By myself I have sworn, declares the LORD... I will surely bless you and multiply your offspring'.

systems.name: Divine testing
systems.ancient_near_east_context: In Israel's tradition God proves a person's loyalty by a demanding command (Gen 22; Exod 16:4; Deut 8:2; 13:3; Job 1-2). The Hebrew verb nissah has the sense of a proof or trial, not a temptation to evil. Child sacrifice is known in the wider region but is condemned elsewhere in the law (Lev 18:21; Deut 12:31).
rules_and_mechanics: God initiates the test and states it as a command.
The test measures fear of God and obedience, not knowledge: the result is described as God coming to know (22:12).
The person has no way to verify the demand and proves himself by acting on it.
God can end the test at the last moment before harm is done.

systems.name: Substitutionary offering
systems.ancient_near_east_context: An animal offered in place of a person or a firstborn is widely attested in the region, and Israelite law redeems the firstborn by substitution (Exod 13:13; 34:20). The ram here stands in the place ('in the stead of his son', 22:13) of the person spared.
rules_and_mechanics: A person is spared and an animal is offered instead.
The substitute is provided from outside the one who offers, here by God.
The offering is carried out in full as a burnt offering on the altar.
The place may be named for what happened there.

system_instances.outcome_summary: God calls Abraham by name, and Abraham answers 'Here I am'. God then tells him to offer up his only son. Abraham obeys without argument.
system_instances.significance_note: The test the whole chapter turns on: whether Abraham's trust in God reaches the son who carries the promise.

system_instances.outcome_summary: At the place God named, Abraham builds the altar and arranges the wood on it.
system_instances.significance_note: Marks the point of no return: everything is ready for the offering.

system_instances.outcome_summary: God promises Abraham blessing and offspring as many as the stars and the sand, victory over enemies, and blessing for all nations through his seed.
system_instances.significance_note: Restates the promises of Gen 12, 15 and 17 as an oath, now tied to Abraham's obedience.

system_instances.outcome_summary: God commands Abraham to take Isaac to the land of Moriah and offer him there on a mountain God will show.
system_instances.significance_note: The command stacks four descriptions of Isaac (son, only son, whom you love, Isaac), each making the cost greater.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Abraham binds Isaac, lays him on the altar over the wood, and takes the knife to slaughter him. The offering is stopped by the angel before the blow.
system_instances.significance_note: The climax of the chapter and the only place in the Hebrew Bible where the binding (akedah) of a person for offering is told this way.

system_instances.outcome_summary: The angel of the LORD calls Abraham twice from heaven, forbids him to harm the boy, and declares that Abraham now has proved he fears God.
system_instances.significance_note: God turns back his own command at the last moment, and the promise through Isaac is kept.

system_instances.outcome_summary: The angel calls a second time from heaven and speaks for the LORD: 'By myself I have sworn', since Abraham did not withhold his son.
system_instances.significance_note: The only place in Genesis where God swears by himself to Abraham; the oath rests on Abraham's obedience.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Abraham names the place 'The LORD will provide', and the text says the saying is still current 'to this day'.
system_instances.significance_note: Fixes the lesson of the chapter in a name and gives the site a later cultic use.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Abraham burns the ram whole on the altar as a burnt offering.
system_instances.significance_note: The offering the command asked for is carried out, with the ram in the son's place.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Abraham sees a ram caught by its horns in a thicket and offers it in place of his son.
system_instances.significance_note: The sign that God does provide, answering Abraham's words in 22:8; the substitute is supplied, not chosen.

edges.description: Abraham ties Isaac and lays him on the altar on top of the wood.
Abraham tells his two servants to stay with the donkey while he and Isaac go on to worship.
Abraham lays the wood for the burnt offering on Isaac while he himself carries the fire and the knife.
Abraham calls the place 'The LORD will provide'.
Abraham takes the ram and offers it as a burnt offering in place of his son.
Abraham stretches out his hand and takes the knife to slaughter his son.
The angel promises Abraham blessing, countless offspring and possession of his enemies' gate.
The angel of the LORD calls from heaven and forbids Abraham to lay a hand on the boy or do anything to him.
The angel declares that the LORD has sworn by himself because Abraham did not withhold his only son.
The report to Abraham notes that Bethuel became the father of Rebekah, the future wife of Isaac.
God tells Abraham to take his only son Isaac to Moriah and offer him as a burnt offering.
Isaac asks his father where the lamb for the burnt offering is, since they have the fire and the wood.
God supplies a ram caught in a thicket, fulfilling Abraham's words that God will provide the lamb.
